title: Formic-acid dehydrogenation reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed thermal-catalyst family for liquid organic hydrogen carrier screening around formic-acid dehydrogenation. These candidates compare a practical Pd/C anchor with newer non-noble and Pt-Mo ensemble routes that target faster hydrogen release or lower noble-metal intensity.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance catalyst cost, evidence quality, route maturity, and reported performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward catalyst cost while preserving route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward transparent pricing anchors and more reproducible preparation routes.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2023
citations.note: Pt-Mo ensemble catalyst reported for highly efficient gas-phase formic-acid dehydrogenation with minimal CO production.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2024
citations.note: Mechanistic study clarifying how palladium surfaces mediate low-temperature formic-acid dehydrogenation pathways.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2024
citations.note: Co single-atoms plus nanoparticles on N-doped carbon reported as a non-noble route for formic-acid dehydrogenation.

citations.label: Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2008
citations.note: Loges, Boddien & Junge: room-temperature hydrogen generation from formic-acid amine adducts, demonstrated through H2/O2 fuel-cell coupling.

citations.label: Science 2011
citations.note: Boddien, Mellmann, Gartner et al.: efficient iron-based homogeneous catalyst for formic-acid dehydrogenation, establishing non-noble-metal viability.

citations.label: Nature Nanotechnology 2011
citations.note: Tedsree, Li, Jones et al.: Ag-Pd core-shell nanocatalyst enabling room-temperature gas-phase formic-acid decomposition with selective H2 generation.

citations.label: Chem. Soc. Rev. 2016
citations.note: Mellmann, Sponholz, Junge and Beller: foundational review of formic acid as a hydrogen-storage medium, surveying homogeneous catalysts for selective H2 release.

route_templates.name: Pd/C dehydrogenation route
route_templates.route_note: Closest screening proxy to practical supported-Pd formic-acid dehydrogenation catalysts.

route_templates.name: Co-NC non-noble route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Pyrolyzed Co single-atom and nanoparticle route
route_templates.route_note: Attractive non-noble option for hydrogen-carrier screening, but pyrolysis and acid-wash discipline reduce route maturity.

route_templates.name: Pt-Mo ensemble route
route_templates.route_note: High-performance premium route when cleaner gas-phase H2 release matters more than absolute catalyst cost.

candidates.title: Pd/C baseline
candidates.summary: Supported palladium route used as a practical anchor for formic-acid dehydrogenation screening.
decision_notes: Best fit when a familiar and defensible supported-Pd screening anchor is needed for LOHC hydrogen-release work.
Palladium keeps route maturity high, but catalyst economics remain exposed to precious-metal pricing.

pricing.note: Live palladium feed with precursor conversion markup.

Activated-carbon support price held on an engineering proxy for hydrogen-carrier screening. Bracketed by public references: UN Comtrade 2024 U.S. carbon-black import unit value ~$1.88/kg (~$0.85/lb rubber grade) and Fuel Cell Store Vulcan XC-72R lab retail ~$950/kg. Bulk conductive/acetylene battery grades cluster at $5,000-7,000/t in marketplace offers (MOQ 1-2 t), the tier between rubber grade and lab retail.

candidates.title: Co-SAs/NPs@NC route
candidates.summary: Cobalt single-atom and nanoparticle route on N-doped carbon for lower-cost formic-acid dehydrogenation screening.
decision_notes: Useful when the program goal is to avoid palladium while keeping hydrogen-release performance credible.
Pyrolysis and acid-wash complexity reduce reproducibility versus the supported-Pd baseline.

pricing.note: Live cobalt feed with precursor conversion markup.
N-doped carbon host held on an engineering proxy until a cleaner public bulk basis is curated.

candidates.title: Pt-Mo ensemble route
candidates.summary: Pt-Mo ensemble catalyst emphasizing gas-phase hydrogen release with very low CO impurity.
decision_notes: Best used when gas-phase formic-acid dehydrogenation and very low CO are worth a platinum premium.
Pt and Mo ensemble control improves the performance score but keeps the route less mature than supported Pd.
